fixes.explanation: Twelve is a fair guess, baker. But Zechariah says the lampstand has "…seven lamps on it, with seven spouts to the lamps." (Zechariah 4:2) So it's seven, not twelve. Counting lamps in a vision is hard work, and I'd have lost track too.

Ten is a nice round number, and I get why it feels right. But Zechariah says the lampstand has "…seven lamps on it, with seven spouts to the lamps." (Zechariah 4:2) Seven lamps, each with its own spout. Ten isn't the count he gives.

Fig trees are a good guess, but they aren't in this vision. Zechariah says, "There are also two olive trees beside it, one on the right side of the bowl and the other on its left." (Zechariah 4:3) So these two are olive trees. He'd just been woken from his sleep (Zechariah 4:1), and I'd have mixed up the trees too.

That's it. The word says, "Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts." (Zechariah 4:6) The LORD is the one speaking, so "My Spirit" means His Spirit. Zerubbabel gets the message straight from the LORD.

A decree sounds official, I'll give it that. But the word to Zerubbabel says, "Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts." (Zechariah 4:6) So it's by the LORD's Spirit, not by a decree. That's the whole point of the message.

Joshua is a fair guess, baker. But this word is spoken "to Zerubbabel," and it says, "Then he will bring forth the capstone accompanied by shouts of ‘Grace, grace to it!’…" (Zechariah 4:6-7) So the one bringing it forth is Zerubbabel. Joshua isn't named in this passage.

Rejoice, that's the word. "…these seven eyes of the LORD, which scan the whole earth, will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel." (Zechariah 4:10) A plumb line is a builder's tool, so that's a happy sight for the eyes. I like that picture of eyes rejoicing over a plumb line.

Water is a fair guess for something pouring from pipes. But Zechariah asks about "…the two gold pipes from which the golden oil pours?" (Zechariah 4:12) So it's golden oil, not water. The verse names oil, and that's what's pouring.

Watchmen on a wall, huh? I can see them up there squinting at the horizon. But the angel says, "These are the two anointed ones who are standing beside the Lord of all the earth." (Zechariah 4:14) They're anointed ones, and they stand beside the Lord. No wall in that verse, so those watchmen can clock out.

Guards at a gate, huh? You went full security team on me, baker. But the angel says, "These are the two anointed ones who are standing beside the Lord of all the earth." (Zechariah 4:14) They're called anointed ones, and they stand beside the Lord. The verse says nothing about a gate or any guarding.
